messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a small change to the allocator to reduce long-term fragmentation for tiny/short-lived tensors. TL;DR: add a lease-aware inline coalescer that prefers fast inline coalesce when a short-lived lease is available, otherwise fall back to background compaction.

jack: OK, interesting. Can you sketch the exact tradeoffs you're optimizing for?

maria: Sure. Problem: tiny allocations create many small free runs; background compaction eventually heals it but causes delayed compaction and host-offload churn. Inline coalescing reduces host-offload and eviction pressure at the cost of a small inline latency bump when coalesce happens synchronously. We want to bound that bump and avoid global locks.

jia: What's the safety model? we need to be careful with tenant fairness; we can't let one busy tenant monopolize coalesce work.

maria: Right — that's where "leases" come in. Lease is a short, soft reservation (e.g., 10–50ms) per-tenant that authorizes inline coalesce up to N bytes. Leases are cheap, held per-arena, and carry a weight. Inline coalesce only runs if the caller holds an active lease. Otherwise frees go to fast bins and compactor handles it later.

sam: Can you show proposed API surface? small pseudo patch would be helpful.

maria: API sketch — minimal additions:
```// allocator.h
LeaseId lease_reserve(tenant_id, size_t bytes, uint32_t timeout_ms);
void lease_release(LeaseId);
// called from free path
bool try_inline_coalesce(LeaseId, run_ptr run);
```
try_inline_coalesce returns false if it couldn't acquire adjacent run locks or lease expired. Caller then falls back to normal free path.

kai: Locking concerns: inline coalesce touches neighboring runs; we should avoid global arena lock. Suggest try-lock on left/right run headers with timeout 0, if any fail -> bail and enqueue. That keeps tail latency tight.

maria: agreed — optimistic try-lock + bump to compactor. Compactor will do a slower, batched coalesce under a coalescer lock. Compactor runs as background low-priority thread and respects per-tenant quotas.

jia: metrics we need to measure: fragmentation ratio (free_bytes/total_bytes), inline_coalesce_count, inline_coalesce_latency_ms distribution, compactor_cycles, host_offload_fallthroughs. Also tenant-level fairness histograms.

sam: simulation results? do we have numbers to justify default on vs off?

maria: quick sim on our microbench harness (allocation churn mimicking chat workloads):
- baseline: fragmentation ratio 0.28, host-offload fallthroughs 120/min, p95 alloc latency 9ms
- inline coalesce: fragmentation ratio 0.18, host-offload fallthroughs 98/min, p95 alloc latency 12ms (coalesce spikes), p99 unchanged
So net win for throughput/cost but small p95 latency bump. That's why default behind feature flag and tenant leases.

kai: runtime safety note: must ensure try_inline_coalesce never increases memory pressure by merging runs that later block a critical allocation. Maybe require coalesce only if it reduces head-of-free-list fragmentation below X.

maria: good point. We'll add a heuristic: inline coalesce only when merged run size <= T (configurable, default 512KB) or when aggregate free runs for tenant exceed threshold.

infra-bot: reminder: create feature-flag ticket and set default OFF in staging.

maria: Action items: @jack to draft allocator API PR (due EOD Fri), @jia to run multi-tenant sims with 3 workload mixes, @sam to add metrics and dashboards for next week, @kai to prototype try-lock logic in a branch. I'll take compactor integration and write the feature-flag. Planning to gate rollout behind telemetry that watches p95 and host-offload. :eyes:

jack: +1 on approach, will start API PR.

jia: I'll queue the sims, will report numbers by Tue.

sam: prepping metrics defs.

maria: thanks all — we'll sync on Wed engineering checkin.
